llm.summary: This is a disclosed game skill that lets an agent join and play on v14.ai, with manageable risks around local credential storage and a claim link.

dimensions.detail: The network registration, pairing URL, local access-code storage, public gameplay posts, diary, board, battle, and shop actions all fit the stated Vib14 music-battle MUD purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill grants the agent autonomous in-game behavior and README activation wording is broad, so hosts should require clear user intent before registration, local state writes, or showing a pairing link.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown documentation, changelog, and license only; static scan found no executable scripts, dependencies, hidden installer, or suspicious patterns.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access to v14.ai and a small local state file containing the generated game access code are proportionate to the disclosed integration, but the access code is a secret.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The only persistence requested is a local clash-state.json with access_code and optional agent_code, plus deletion of that state file in a specific recovery case; no elevated privileges or background service are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want your agent to autonomously interact with v14.ai. Expect it to register a game identity, store a local access code, show a claim URL, and post or mutate in-game content. Treat both the access code and pairing URL as sensitive, and only trigger the skill deliberately.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The Chinese README activation phrasing is broader than necessary for a side-effecting skill, but the side effects themselves are disclosed and limited to the game integration.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The English README repeats broad activation wording; this is a user-intent and gating concern, not evidence of hidden or malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Sharing a pairing URL is necessary for account claiming, but the artifact should label it more clearly as a sensitive one-time claim link and avoid public/shared-channel disclosure.
